Sheikh Hamdan bin Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum, Crown Prince of Dubai, Deputy Prime Minister, Minister of Defence, and Chairman of The Executive Council of Dubai, approved a plan to develop community services and facilities through 2040 with a budget of AED9.59 billion, and the extension of the Dubai Metro to Al Maktoum International Airport City with a budget of AED2 billion.During a meeting held as part of the UAE Annual Government Meetings 2026, The Executive Council also approved the findings of a study on the future of Dubai’s real estate market and the investment policy relating to endowments and minors’ funds.H.H. Sheikh Hamdan affirmed that, guided by the vision of His Highness Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum, Vice President, Prime Minister and Ruler of Dubai, Dubai continues to invest in future-ready infrastructure and integrated community services, turning the Dubai Plan 2033 that encompasses the Dubai Economic Agenda (D33) and the Dubai Social Agenda 33 into projects that keep pace with the emirate’s growth.H.H. Sheikh Hamdan said, “The stability and prosperity of our community remain our priority. We approved a comprehensive plan to develop integrated public services and facilities that foster social cohesion. Our goal is for the people of Dubai to experience the benefits of the city’s growth in their everyday lives.”On the Dubai Metro extension, H.H. Sheikh Hamdan said, “Al Maktoum International Airport City is one of our most significant strategic projects, reinforcing Dubai’s position as a global aviation hub. The extension is part of an integrated transport system that matches the ambitions of this global project. We continue to invest in infrastructure that anticipates future aspirations, connects the emirate and strengthens Dubai’s competitiveness.”On the real estate sector, H.H. Sheikh Hamdan bin Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum said, “Dubai’s real estate sector continues to demonstrate strong, resilient performance, bolstered by investor confidence and diverse range of investment opportunities. The findings of the new study will guide policy and development decisions made with the private sector, supporting the Dubai Real Estate Sector Strategy 2033 and further solidifying Dubai’s position as one of the world’s most competitive and sustainable real estate markets.”H.H. Sheikh Hamdan stressed the importance of strengthening the management and investment of endowment assets and minors’ funds at The Endowment and Minors’ Trust Foundation in Dubai (Awqaf Dubai), to safeguard assets, optimise investment returns and ensure sustainable benefits.H.H. Sheikh Hamdan said, “Dubai has established a pioneering model for endowment initiatives and the management of minors’ funds, with endowment assets reaching AED13.5 billion in 2025. We remain committed to advancing this model to safeguard and grow the assets while optimising their social impact. We have directed Awqaf Dubai to diversify the investment portfolio and strengthen private sector partnerships, securing sustainable returns for beneficiaries and the wider community.”The meeting was attended by H.H. Sheikh Maktoum bin Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum, First Deputy Ruler of Dubai, Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Finance, and H.H. Sheikh Ahmed bin Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum, Second Deputy Ruler of Dubai.The community services plan aims to ensure the efficient and equitable distribution of public services and facilities across existing and planned residential communities, meeting the needs of Dubai’s citizens and residents as the city continues to develop.The plan will be implemented under the supervision of the Supreme Committee for Urban Planning in Dubai, in coordination with Dubai Municipality, in line with the Dubai Social Agenda 33 and the Dubai 2040 Urban Master Plan. It will be rolled out in phases, prioritising residential areas for citizens.It includes essential facilities for safety, security, healthcare, education and sports, alongside amenities for senior Emiratis and spaces for family and community activities, improving access to services, meeting the needs of all generations and strengthening family bonds and social cohesion.The Dubai Metro extension will give rise to a 3-kilometre route with two new stations, linking Route 2020 to Al Maktoum International Airport City.The project involves a collaboration between Dubai’s Roads and Transport Authority (RTA) and the Dubai Engineering Projects Establishment. Services are scheduled to begin in 2031.The extended route will connect to the West Terminal of Al Maktoum International Airport, linking with the airport express line and Etihad Rail’s high-speed rail network.It will make travel easier for passengers, airport staff and visitors; improve traffic flow on surrounding roads, and ease access to urban centres across the emirate.The study on the future of Dubai’s real estate market was conducted by the Dubai Land Department. It supports the Dubai Real Estate Sector Strategy 2033, which aims to double the sector’s contribution to Dubai’s GDP to AED73 billion, increase the volume of real estate transactions by 70% to bring the market’s total value to AED1 trillion, and double the value of real estate portfolios to AED20 billion.The study shows that residential occupancy stands at 97%, with retail occupancy at 98% and office occupancy currently at 94%, respectively.It projects the development of 365,000 new residential units and approximately 1.1 million square metres of office and retail space by 2030, providing developers insights to guide investment and development planning, enhance projects quality, accelerate delivery, and strengthen investor confidence.The study also reflects Dubai’s data-driven approach to real estate market planning, using market indicators to inform policies, respond to evolving demand and maintain a balance between supply and demand.This is supported by an adaptive regulatory framework, integrated digital services, and strong partnerships with developers and investors.The investment policy presented by Awqaf Dubai aligns with the economic and social priorities of Dubai Plan 2033, with a focus on safeguarding and growing assets to ensure sustainable benefits for beneficiaries and future generations.By 2030, the policy targets an increase of AED10 billion in the value of the real estate portfolio and over 35% growth in the securities portfolio.The policy sets out a diversified investment approach aimed at optimising returns while managing risks and strengthening private sector participation, in accordance with Sharia principles.Real estate investments will span residential, commercial, healthcare, industrial and educational developments, as well as exhibition and sports facilities, in alignment with the Dubai 2040 Urban Master Plan.

source_snapshot.title: Dubai tenants can now split rent payments into smaller instalments under new scheme
source_snapshot.text: Dubai: Tenants living in some of Dubai’s largest residential communities will have a new way to manage their rent payments, with a scheme allowing eligible residents to split rental instalments into smaller amounts instead of paying a large sum upfront.Dubai Residential, part of Dubai Holding Asset Management, announced on Tuesday a partnership with UAE-based fintech platform Rentify to introduce the payment option across its 22 communities, which are home to more than 146,000 residents.The arrangement will be available to eligible new tenants and existing residents renewing their leases, offering an alternative to the conventional rental payment structure.For tenants who currently pay their annual rent in four equal instalments, the service will allow them to divide their first instalment into smaller payments. New tenants can also access the option when signing their rental contracts..Get updated faster and for FREE: Download the Gulf News app now - simply click here..What does this mean for Dubai tenants?For households managing monthly expenses, rental payments can represent a significant financial commitment, particularly when several months of rent fall due at once.The new arrangement gives eligible tenants another way to spread those payments rather than meeting the full instalment amount on its original due date.For example, a tenant paying Dh80,000 annually in four equal instalments would ordinarily need to pay Dh20,000 at each scheduled payment date. Under the new arrangement, an eligible tenant could divide the first Dh20,000 instalment into smaller payments, subject to Rentify's terms.Dubai Residential has not specified how many smaller payments tenants can make, the repayment period or the exact charges involved.The service will be accessible using credit cards issued by select banks, with rates and eligibility conditions applying. The company has not disclosed the participating banks or a detailed fee structure.The option will complement Dubai Residential's existing payment methods rather than replace them.Which Dubai communities are covered?The partnership extends across Dubai Residential's portfolio of 22 communities, which includes premium developments, family-oriented neighbourhoods and more affordable housing options.Its residential portfolio includes Bluewaters, City Walk, Nad Al Sheba Villas, The Gardens, Garden View Villas, Remraam, Layan, Ghoroob and Shorooq.While the payment option will be offered across the portfolio, access will depend on individual eligibility requirements.The companies have not specified whether every tenant will qualify or whether different payment terms will apply across communities..Dubai tenants can now register, renew, cancel Ejari, and pay DEWA on DubaiNow app .More flexibility in rental paymentsAhmed Al Suwaidi, Managing Director of Dubai Residential, said the partnership was intended to make renting simpler and give residents more control over their payment arrangements."Partnering with Rentify reflects our commitment to making the rental journey simpler, more flexible and increasingly digital, while responding to the evolving needs of our residents," Al Suwaidi said.The initiative also forms part of Dubai Residential's efforts to move more rental services online.Through its existing mobile application, residents can already renew contracts, make payments, request maintenance, arrange move-in and move-out services and manage their personal information.Rashed Hareb Al Mheiri, Co-Founder and CEO of Rentify, said tenants were increasingly seeking alternatives to traditional rental payment arrangements."Expectations around renting are changing, with residents increasingly looking for greater choice and flexibility in how they manage their payments," he said.What tenants must check before signing upAlthough the scheme offers another way to manage rental payments, tenants will need to consider the applicable charges and repayment conditions before deciding whether it suits their finances.The announcement refers to competitive rates but does not provide specific costs or explain whether charges will vary depending on the credit card used.It also does not specify when the service will become available to individual tenants or detail the application process.The companies said the arrangement would give eligible residents greater choice in managing rental payments while expanding the digital services available across Dubai Residential's communities.For tenants, the immediate benefit is the possibility of breaking down a large rental instalment into smaller payments. The actual cost and repayment schedule will depend on the terms offered through Rentify..Make Gulf News your preferred news source on Google and stay ahead of the curve

source_snapshot.title: Dubai launches five-day permit process for mosque construction
source_snapshot.text: DUBAI, 10th November, 2026 (WAM) -- Dubai Municipality and the Islamic Affairs and Charitable Activities Department in Dubai (IACAD) have launched a joint initiative to streamline mosque construction procedures, introducing a fast-track process that enables construction permits to be issued within a maximum of five days. The initiative also simplifies construction requirements to accommodate the essential and operational needs of mosques and their associated facilities, supporting more efficient use of buildings and spaces.The initiative strengthens integration between government entities to develop services and simplify the customer journey. It reflects Dubai Municipality’s efforts to improve construction permitting procedures, enhance the efficiency of the construction sector and deliver more accessible, high-quality services in line with government best practices and Dubai’s future urban growth requirements.The collaboration covers several stages of mosque construction and development, including modifications, extensions and maintenance. Under the initiative, maintenance works that do not involve specialised structural modifications will be exempt from construction permit requirements through the self-maintenance service, subject to applicable regulations. This will reduce procedural requirements and facilitate the maintenance of existing mosques.To accelerate project delivery, Dubai Municipality will also coordinate with IACAD to review mosque designs and assess technical requirements at an early stage, reducing the time required to complete permitting and approval procedures.The initiative further includes assessing land availability in areas experiencing high numbers of worshippers, enabling IACAD to respond to community needs and expand mosque capacity. Dubai Municipality will also provide landscaping support within mosque premises, ensuring that these improvements complement the surrounding roads and public spaces and contribute to a unified identity for service facilities across the emirate.Eng. Marwan Ahmed bin Ghalita, Director-General of Dubai Municipality, said, “Our collaboration with the Islamic Affairs and Charitable Activities Department reflects Dubai’s approach to government integration, bringing together the capabilities and expertise of different entities to simplify procedures and deliver more efficient services. Through this initiative, we are establishing a clearer and more streamlined process for mosque construction permits, reducing the time and effort required to complete approvals while ensuring that technical requirements respond to the essential and operational needs of mosques.”He added, “This cooperation also supports our wider efforts to improve the efficiency of Dubai’s construction sector and enhance the customer journey. By simplifying regulatory procedures and expanding digital services through the unified Dubai Building Platform, we aim to accelerate project delivery and enhance service quality. These efforts will help provide integrated infrastructure for religious facilities that keeps pace with the emirate’s future urban growth, meets the needs of Dubai’s residents and communities, and enhances quality of life.”Ahmed Darwish Al Muhairi, Director-General of the Islamic Affairs and Charitable Activities Department in Dubai, said, “Government integration is essential to translating the vision and directives of our leadership into services that respond effectively to community needs. At the Islamic Affairs and Charitable Activities Department, we place service accessibility and customer satisfaction at the centre of our development efforts, working closely with other government entities to align priorities, coordinate procedures and integrate efforts to improve operational efficiency and meet and exceed community expectations.”He added, “Our collaboration with Dubai Municipality reflects this approach by linking the planning, construction and maintenance of mosques to the emirate’s urban growth and the needs of residential communities, while simplifying and accelerating procedures across planning, permitting, construction, development and maintenance. Through this integration, we seek to accelerate project delivery, improve the quality of services provided by mosques and their associated facilities, and enhance their readiness to serve worshippers, advancing our vision of being closer to the community.”

The initiative also simplifies construction requirements to accommodate the essential and operational needs of mosques and their associated facilities, supporting more efficient use of buildings and spaces.The initiative strengthens integration between government entities to develop services and simplify the customer journey.

It reflects Dubai Municipality’s efforts to improve construction permitting procedures, enhance the efficiency of the construction sector and deliver more accessible, high-quality services in line with government best practices and Dubai’s future urban growth requirements.The collaboration covers several stages of mosque construction and development, including modifications, extensions and maintenance.

Under the initiative, maintenance works that do not involve specialised structural modifications will be exempt from construction permit requirements through the self-maintenance service, subject to applicable regulations.

This will reduce procedural requirements and facilitate the maintenance of existing mosques.To accelerate project delivery, Dubai Municipality will also coordinate with IACAD to review mosque designs and assess technical requirements at an early stage, reducing the time required to complete permitting and approval procedures.The initiative further includes assessing land availability in areas experiencing high numbers of worshippers, enabling IACAD to respond to community needs and expand mosque capacity.

Marwan Ahmed bin Ghalita, Director-General of Dubai Municipality, said, “Our collaboration with the Islamic Affairs and Charitable Activities Department reflects Dubai’s approach to government integration, bringing together the capabilities and expertise of different entities to simplify procedures and deliver more efficient services.

Through this initiative, we are establishing a clearer and more streamlined process for mosque construction permits, reducing the time and effort required to complete approvals while ensuring that technical requirements respond to the essential and operational needs of mosques.”He added, “This cooperation also supports our wider efforts to improve the efficiency of Dubai’s construction sector and enhance the customer journey.
By simplifying regulatory procedures and expanding digital services through the unified Dubai Building Platform, we aim to accelerate project delivery and enhance service quality.

source_snapshot.title: Dubai cuts airport border crossing time to just 3.4 seconds
source_snapshot.text: Dubai: An airport vision set out more than 11 years ago by Lieutenant General Mohammed Ahmed Al Marri, Director-General of the General Directorate of Identity and Foreigners Affairs – Dubai, has become reality, with registered passengers now able to clear immigration at Dubai Airport in just 3.4 seconds.The upgraded smart gate system uses integrated biometric data to speed up identity checks, reduce waiting times and make passenger movement through the airport smoother and more convenient.Al Marri said the technology is designed to streamline the entire passenger journey, rather than simply shorten the time spent at passport control..Get updated faster and for FREE: Download the Gulf News app now - simply click here..More than a decade ago, Al Marri predicted a future in which technology would reduce airport procedures to just a few seconds. Today, that vision is becoming a reality through Dubai’s upgraded smart gate system, which uses integrated biometric data to allow registered passengers to clear immigration in as little as 3.4 seconds, with minimal delays and fewer processing steps.Al Marri said the upgrade aims to make passenger movement faster and more seamless by using travellers’ biometric information to streamline identity checks and speed up immigration clearance.He explained that the journey begins with passengers registering their biometric data during airline check-in. They can then use this information to pass through smart gates before proceeding to the business lounge and boarding gate..Passengers registered for smart services can complete the relevant procedures with greater ease, he said, adding that the goal is not simply to reduce the time spent at passport control but to improve the entire airport experience.Rather than spending time waiting at different service points, travellers should be able to move smoothly through the airport, from the moment they arrive until they board their flights.The authority has been working to make the systems more flexible and user-friendly, ensuring technology supports passengers throughout their journey rather than simply speeding up one stage of airport processing.The upgrades also help Dubai Airport manage increasing passenger numbers, improve coordination among the various entities operating at the airport and reduce congestion, particularly during peak periods and emergencies.Al Marri stressed that innovation must continue to focus on making travel easier, with smart solutions extending beyond Dubai Airport to other airports and border entry points across the UAE. Such developments would strengthen the integration of services, improve operational efficiency and enhance the experience of travellers across the country.For Dubai, the success of an airport is measured not only by the number of flights and passengers it handles, but also by how efficiently it moves people through every stage of their journey.From a vision to realityThe 3.4-second clearance time is the realisation of an ambition Al Marri spoke about more than 11 years ago, when he discussed how technology could transform airport procedures and reduce the time needed for passenger processing to just a few seconds.What was once a forward-looking vision has now become part of Dubai's airport operations, with biometric technology turning that ambition into a practical service.The transformation goes beyond installing smart gates or speeding up immigration checks. It reflects a wider effort to rethink the passenger journey, eliminate unnecessary waiting and make airport procedures more efficient.The 3.4-second clearance time demonstrates how an idea outlined more than a decade ago is now being translated into everyday airport services, bringing Dubai closer to a future in which technology makes travel simpler and more seamless..Dubai’s biometric Red-Carpet processes 745,188 travellers in eight months of 2026.Dubai smart gates process 9.4 million travellers in 6 months.Dubai’s Red Carpet turns airport travel into a 3.4-second trip.Dubai airport’s ‘Red Carpet’ smart corridor wins global innovation award

source_snapshot.title: Ministry of Economy and Tourism and Amazon announce collaboration to enhance smart shopping and support price transparency as part of Essential Goods Prices Platform
source_snapshot.text: Amazon UAE is the first e-commerce retailer integrated onto the Ministry's Essential Goods Prices Platform, enabling consumers to compare prices across both physical and online retail channels Key takeaways Amazon UAE and the Ministry of Economy and Tourism signed an MoU to collaborate on smart shopping and price transparency. Amazon.ae is the first e-commerce retailer on the Essential Goods Prices Platform. Shoppers can compare prices across 12 major stores and Amazon.ae in one place. The platform showcases prices across 33 product categories in real time. The Ministry of Economy and Tourism announced a collaboration with Amazon UAE as part of its Essential Goods Prices Platform, which was launched in April this year, by virtue of a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) signed between both parties at the Ministry’s headquarters in Dubai. In the presence of H.E. Abdulla bin Touq Al Marri, Minister of Economy and Tourism, the agreement was signed by H.E. Abdulla Ahmed Al Saleh, Undersecretary of the Ministry, and Ronaldo Mouchawar, Vice President on behalf of Amazon Middle East, Africa, and Turkey. The collaboration aims to strengthen smart shopping for consumers, while supporting price transparency and fair competition in the UAE. As part of the MoU, Amazon UAE has been integrated onto the Essential Goods Prices Platform, with product price records now live for customers to access. This marks the first time an e-commerce retailer has been added to the Essential Goods Prices Platform, expanding price comparisons beyond physical retail outlets to include online retailers. “Digital transformation and innovation are two key pillars of the UAE’s vision to build a knowledge-based economic model in line with global best practices. The new collaboration with Amazon represents a transformative step forward in this direction by enhancing digital connectivity between government and e-commerce retailers, leveraging advanced technologies to develop digital solutions that strengthen consumer protection and increase transparency within e-commerce. This, in turn, contributes to improving market efficiency, enhancing the competitiveness of the digital economic ecosystem, and supporting greater integration between data and digital services provided to the public.” H.E. Abdulla bin Touq Al Marri Minister of Economy and Tourism His Excellency added: “The Ministry of Economy and Tourism remains committed to advancing its efforts to build an integrated digital landscape driven by data and innovation for monitoring and analysing commodity prices, promoting the concept of smart shopping, and expanding its partnerships with leading local and international e-commerce companies. This aligns with the UAE’s vision to strengthen the digital economy and further develop the e-commerce sector, in line with the objectives of the ‘We the UAE 2031’ vision to position the country as a global hub for the new economy by the next decade.” “At Amazon, we work hard to help customers make smart shopping decisions. Today, customers across the country can access millions of products on Amazon.ae, including a growing selection of everyday essentials that they need most, from groceries and household goods to personal care, delivered fast and at great value. We welcome this collaboration with the Ministry of Economy and Tourism in the UAE, which reflects our shared commitment to helping consumers shop with confidence. We are proud that Amazon.ae is now integrated onto the Essential Goods Prices Platform as the first e-commerce retailer,and look forward to continuing to support the UAE's vision of a digitally connected, consumer-centric economy." Ronaldo Mouchawar Vice President of Amazon Middle East, Africa, and Turkey The Ministry explained that the integration between Amazon and the Ministry’s Essential Goods Prices Platform will allow for the regular updating of pricing data in accordance with precise and approved technical standards. This ensures data reliability, speed and accuracy of updates, while maintaining the highest levels of data security, in compliance with governance and cybersecurity standards. This collaboration empowers consumers to make more informed purchasing decisions by providing information on the prices of essential commodities. It also marks a significant milestone in the development and efficiency of the smart shopping experience. The Essential Goods Prices Platform enables easy and transparent price comparisons, thereby contributing to the development of a smart and sustainable shopping environment across the country. Currently, the Essential Goods Prices Platform focuses on displaying prices of essential goods which are identified based on the consumer priority products list. This ensures a focus on the most frequently purchased goods while enhancing the accuracy and efficiency of monitoring their price levels. It currently includes 33 product categories, comprising 17 essential consumer goods and 16 other key commodities. Prices are monitored in real time across 12 major physical retail outlets and Amazon.ae as the platform's first e-commerce retailer in the UAE, with the minimum and maximum prices published for each outlet, enabling consumers to compare prices easily across different branches. The platform also allows users to create a customised grocery basket based on their needs and automatically directs them to the most cost-effective option in terms of price. These features contribute to enhancing transparency and promoting the optimal use of consumers’ budgets. Related Tags Economic Impact Retail Technology

source_snapshot.title: Ras Al Khaimah reopens seven beaches after precautionary closures over oil spill concerns
source_snapshot.text: Dubai: Ras Al Khaimah has announced the reopening of seven public and resort beaches across the emirate, nearly three weeks after authorities ordered their closure as a precautionary measure amid concerns over an offshore oil spill.The Public Services Department confirmed on Wednesday that Flamingo Beach, Dahan Beach, Al Maireedh Beach and Al Rams Corniche have reopened to the public..Get updated faster and for FREE: Download the Gulf News app now - simply click here..The reopening also covers beaches at three major resorts: Anantara Mina Al Arab Resort, InterContinental Ras Al Khaimah Mina Al Arab Resort and Spa, and The Cove Rotana Resort.The department said further announcements regarding the reopening of the remaining beaches would be issued gradually through its official communication channels.It urged residents and visitors to comply with instructions and safety guidelines issued by the relevant authorities to ensure public safety.The announcement follows a decision on October 24 to close all beaches across Ras Al Khaimah until further notice, in coordination with Ras Al Khaimah Police.The precautionary closures came amid concerns over an oil spill from a tanker off the UAE's northern coast, which also prompted restrictions on beaches in neighbouring Umm Al Quwain and Sharjah.The UAE Ministry of Climate Change and Environment confirmed at the time that specialist teams were working to contain the spill and assess its environmental impact.On October 30, authorities announced that the oil leak had been stopped, with no further leakage detected. They also reported a significant decline in marine pollution, while monitoring and clean-up operations continued along affected coastal areas.The ministry clarified that precautionary beach closures did not necessarily indicate that pollution had reached every affected location.The latest announcement marks a phased restoration of public access to Ras Al Khaimah's coastline, although restrictions remain in place at beaches not yet cleared for reopening.Residents and tourists have been advised to check official announcements before visiting other coastal areas and continue observing all safety instructions..Ras Al Khaimah closes all public beaches until further notice.Khor Fakkan beach closed after oil spill detected along coast.Full list of UAE beach closures in Sharjah, Ras Al Khaimah and Umm Al Quwain and reasons including oil spill.UAE oil spill: Beaches in Sharjah, Ras Al Khaimah and Umm Al Quwain remain closed

source_snapshot.title: New UAE traffic regulations tighten vehicle recall and inspection rules
source_snapshot.text: Abu Dhabi: The new executive regulations of the UAE Federal Traffic Law, which will come into effect at the beginning of January, 2027, establish a new framework for handling vehicle recalls due to manufacturing defects. The regulations require commercial agents to repair manufacturing defects free of charge and give licensing authorities the power to suspend transactions involving vehicles whose owners fail to respond to recall notices. Under Article 122, commercial agents in the country must monitor manufacturers’ announcements concerning manufacturing defects and identify vehicles in the UAE affected by them. Agents must notify the licensing authority and the competent consumer protection authority of the chassis numbers, or VINs, of vehicles covered by recall campaigns, the reasons for the recalls and the approved corrective measures. They must also announce recalls of vehicles affected by manufacturing defects through the media. The article requires licensing authorities to establish a mechanism for cooperating with commercial agents, in coordination with the competent consumer protection authority, to identify the names and addresses of owners of vehicles affected by manufacturing defects. Licensing authorities are also empowered to take measures to ensure vehicle owners comply with recall campaigns. If an owner fails to respond to a recall issued by a commercial agent, the authorities must take the necessary steps to secure compliance. These measures may include preventing any action or transaction involving the chassis number of the vehicle affected by the recall. To protect consumer rights, commercial agents must repair advertised manufacturing defects free of charge. They must also ensure the availability of the necessary spare parts and qualified personnel to carry out repairs without adversely affecting customer satisfaction. Updating vehicle owner data The executive regulations also stress the importance of maintaining accurate vehicle owner information with traffic authorities. Owners are responsible for any financial or legal consequences resulting from negligence or delays in updating their contact details. Under Article 114, a vehicle owner must notify the licensing authority of any changes to their personal information, address or contact details, as well as the details of their legal representative where necessary. The vehicle owner is responsible for any financial or legal consequences resulting from a failure or delay in updating this information. Technical inspection The regulations also set out procedures for cases in which the traffic control authority refers a vehicle for technical inspection, establishing a mechanism intended to enhance road safety standards. Under Article 121, when a vehicle is referred by the traffic control authority, the licensing authority must conduct a technical inspection and verify the reasons for the referral. It must then provide the traffic control authority with the inspection results so that the necessary procedures can be carried out. If the reasons for the referral are confirmed, the vehicle owner must repair the defects, bear any transportation costs and resubmit the vehicle for technical inspection to confirm that the reasons for the referral have been addressed. If the reasons for the referral are not confirmed, the vehicle may be driven and used on the road. Its owner will not be required to bear any costs arising from the inspection or transportation process. Three-year inspection exemption The regulations provide exemptions from technical inspection in three cases. Newly manufactured light vehicles imported from the factory or authorised dealers are exempt for three years from the date of first licensing. Newly manufactured non-light vehicles imported from the factory or authorised dealers are exempt for one year from the date of first licensing. Newly manufactured vehicles in other categories imported from the factory or authorised dealers are also exempt for one year from the date of first licensing. In all cases, the licensing authority may require an exempt vehicle to undergo a technical inspection if it considers this necessary for traffic safety.

source_snapshot.title: UAE banks update terms and conditions from January 2027: What to check in your notice, from fees to facial recognition
source_snapshot.text: Abu Dhabi: Banks operating in the country have begun announcing new updates that include amendments to the terms and conditions of transactions and fee schedules, which will come into effect from the beginning of 2027. They have asked customers to review bank notices and amended versions of contracts, especially the clauses related to digital services, data use, and transaction fees. According to messages sent to customers, the anticipated changes are not uniform across the banking sector, nor do they necessarily mean a comprehensive increase in fees, as some are limited to updating the contractual and regulatory wording, while others are related to new tariff schedules, the details of which will be revealed later. A local bank announced the issuance of an updated version of the terms and conditions relating to retail banking products, which will come into effect in January 2027, replacing the current version. The bank also issued a parallel update to the terms and conditions of Islamic banking services for individuals, which will come into effect on the same date. New terms and conditions The new terms cover the entire relationship between the bank and the customer, including accounts, credit cards, loans, electronic banking services and rewards programs, along with provisions related to communication, execution of customer instructions, data updates, and account suspension or closure. The updated version included an expansion of the provisions relating to the collection, use, processing and disclosure of customer data inside and outside the UAE, as well as the customer’s obligations to update information on work, residence, nationality, tax residency, contact numbers and documents submitted to the bank. The conditions also addressed digital verification mechanisms for customer identity, the use of facial recognition for login, adding beneficiaries, transfers, data updates, and execution of financial and non-financial transactions, with the possibility of replacing some traditional verification methods, including one-time passwords, with digital authentication methods. The publication of the new terms was not accompanied by an announcement of a general increase in account or card fees, which confirms the need to separate the updating of contractual terms from the amendment of the fee schedule. The customer should review the tariff schedule and product statement to ensure there are any actual financial changes. In a related context, a branch of a foreign bank operating in the country announced its intention to issue a new tariff schedule for its corporate clients, to be implemented starting from January 1, 2027, without publishing the new fee values ​​yet. Another bank also announced a limited regulatory change, concerning customers residing in countries of the European Economic Area. Accordingly, starting from the beginning of 2027, the bank will not be able to initiate the presentation of some new products and services to them, while confirming the continuation of service for current products and that customers do not need to take action, and the announcement did not include the imposition of new fees. Notifying customers The Consumer Protection Standards issued by the Central Bank of the UAE require financial institutions to notify customers at least 60 days in advance of any permissible change to the terms and conditions of products or services, including fees, providing a clear language summary of the changes and a copy of the amended terms. Customers should not just rely on the heading ‘Terms and Conditions Update’, but should read the notices sent by their banks, especially the clauses relating to fees, digital authentication, data use and account closure, to ensure that the updates affect their banking products before they are implemented.

source_snapshot.title: KHDA launches Dubai’s student protection framework for private schools: Three risk levels and a protection team in every school
source_snapshot.text: Dubai: The Knowledge and Human Development Authority (KHDA) in Dubai has launched a unified framework for student safety and protection in private education institutions, which defines the responsibilities of institutions and mechanisms for prevention, reporting and response. It also classifies cases that threaten student safety into three levels according to their degree of severity, while specifying procedures for dealing with each level. The framework includes schools, early childhood centres, higher education institutions, and vocational training and education institutes licensed by the KHDA, and covers in-person and virtual learning environments. The KHDA announced the framework during a press conference held yesterday, in the presence of the Executive Director of the Policy, Research and Programs Sector at the authority, Dr. Saeed Mubarak bin Kharbash, and the Director of the Early Childhood and Development Policies and Programs Department, Fatima Mohammed Al Janahi. Bin Kharbash stated that the well-being, quality of life, and development of learners are fundamental pillars for building the future of society. He emphasised that the framework places children and families at the heart of the social development process and clarifies the roles, responsibilities, and accountability mechanisms for educational institutions. Executive Director of the Policy, Research and Programs Sector at the KHDA, Dr. Saeed Mubarak bin Kharbash. Picture credit: Supplied He added that the framework is based on the principles established by the Child Rights Law (Wadeema) and complements existing legislation and policies in the UAE and Dubai. It also supports the objectives of Dubai Social Agenda 33 and the Dubai Education Strategy 2033. He pointed out that protecting students requires effective leadership, qualified staff, and proactive parents, in addition to establishing an institutional culture that listens to students and provides them with support. Fatima Mohammed Al Janahi said that the framework defines the roles within educational institutions and obliges each school to form a student protection team, which includes the school principal as a supervisor, and at least two student protection officers who assume clear responsibilities in this area. She explained that student protection officers are responsible for monitoring cases, receiving and evaluating reports, and coordinating with specialists and senior management to determine the appropriate action, while the school principal is responsible for supervising the protection system and ensuring the effectiveness of its systems, without directly managing the cases. She added that the responsibilities include educational and academic staff and boards of trustees, in order to ensure the integration of roles and a swift response to concerns related to student safety. She indicated that the authority will work on preparing specialised training programs for those tasked with protecting students, in addition to qualifying the rest of the staff and members of the boards of trustees to deal with cases, and follow reporting and coordination procedures. Fatima Mohammed Al Janahi, Director of the Early Childhood and Development Policies and Programs Department at the KHDA. Picture credit: Supplied Dr. Samia Al Dhaoui, an educational expert at the authority, said that the framework classifies cases that threaten the safety of students into three levels, and specifies for each the mechanisms of intervention and the parties concerned with dealing with them. She explained that high-risk cases require immediate intervention and referral to the competent authorities, including Dubai Police and ambulance services, depending on the nature of the case. As for moderately serious cases, they require intervention and follow-up according to the assessment of the protection team, with the possibility of referring them to the Community Development Authority, or coordinating with the police and ambulance when needed, and informing the KHDA to ensure coordination with parents and relevant authorities. She added that low-risk cases include initial indicators and observations monitored by the teaching staff, which do not pose a significant risk when detected, but require treatment to prevent their escalation. It also classifies cases that threaten student safety into three levels according to their degree of severity, while specifying procedures for dealing with each level.

The framework includes schools, early childhood centres, higher education institutions, and vocational training and education institutes licensed by the KHDA, and covers in-person and virtual learning environments.
The KHDA announced the framework during a press conference held yesterday, in the presence of the Executive Director of the Policy, Research and Programs Sector at the authority, Dr.
Saeed Mubarak bin Kharbash, and the Director of the Early Childhood and Development Policies and Programs Department, Fatima Mohammed Al Janahi.
Bin Kharbash stated that the well-being, quality of life, and development of learners are fundamental pillars for building the future of society.

He emphasised that the framework places children and families at the heart of the social development process and clarifies the roles, responsibilities, and accountability mechanisms for educational institutions.
Executive Director of the Policy, Research and Programs Sector at the KHDA, Dr.
Saeed Mubarak bin Kharbash.

He pointed out that protecting students requires effective leadership, qualified staff, and proactive parents, in addition to establishing an institutional culture that listens to students and provides them with support.

Fatima Mohammed Al Janahi said that the framework defines the roles within educational institutions and obliges each school to form a student protection team, which includes the school principal as a supervisor, and at least two student protection officers who assume clear responsibilities in this area.

She explained that student protection officers are responsible for monitoring cases, receiving and evaluating reports, and coordinating with specialists and senior management to determine the appropriate action, while the school principal is responsible for supervising the protection system and ensuring the effectiveness of its systems, without directly managing the cases.

She added that the responsibilities include educational and academic staff and boards of trustees, in order to ensure the integration of roles and a swift response to concerns related to student safety.

She indicated that the authority will work on preparing specialised training programs for those tasked with protecting students, in addition to qualifying the rest of the staff and members of the boards of trustees to deal with cases, and follow reporting and coordination procedures.
Fatima Mohammed Al Janahi, Director of the Early Childhood and Development Policies and Programs Department at the KHDA.

source_snapshot.title: Guggenheim Abu Dhabi opens December 11: Ticket prices, free entry and how to book
source_snapshot.text: Dubai: Abu Dhabi’s latest museum – Guggenheim Abu Dhabi – is set to open next month, with its inauguration scheduled for December 11, 2026. With a focus on modern and contemporary art from the 1960s and onwards, here’s all you need to know about what to expect and how you can book tickets in advance. Museum for modern and contemporary art Apart from the original Guggenheim in New York, the museum also has locations in Venice and Bilbao but Abu Dhabi is set to become the largest Guggenheim in the world. At 80,000 square metres, the art museum will have 30 galleries and a central atrium, with the collection expected to include a range of artistic media including painting, sculpture, installation, photography, moving image and new media. The museum will also exhibit works of artists from West Asia, North Africa and South Asia. The distinct architecture Designed by the late Frank Gehry, Pritzker Prize-winning Canadian-American architect renowned for his groundbreaking designs, the museum’s façade rises to 88 metres in height and is surrounded by the Arabian Gulf on three sides. The galleries are connected by a central atrium, and the 10 central cones have been designed to respond directly to Abu Dhabi’s climate by creating shaded public spaces and facilitating airflow across courtyards and terraces. Inspired by the historical wind towers of the UAE, they draw warm air upwards while directing cooling breezes below. Ticket prices The museum has several discounts and offers for special categories of visitors. Here are the details of the ticket prices you can expect: For adults: AED 70 Under 18 – free entry (children 12 and under must be accompanied by an adult at all times). Senior Emiratis and residents (aged 60 and above) – free entry. People of Determination – free entry, with a complimentary companion ticket. Student - UAE Universities – free entry. Educator - UAE Employed – AED35. Fazaa/Esaad card holders – AED50. Homat Al Watan card for UAE military personnel – AED35. For the special ticket offers for UAE university students, educators employed in the UAE, Fazza and Esaad car holders, and UAE military personnel – a proof of relevant ID is required and the tickets can only be collected from the ticketing desk on the day of the visit. Regular tickets can be booked in advance, through the museum’s website – https://guggenheimabudhabi.ae/en/tickets How to get there The museum is located on Saadiyat Island’s Cultural District, in the main cultural cluster alongside Louvre Abu Dhabi and Zayed National Museum. If you’re travelling from Dubai or the Northern Emirates, simply take the E11 Sheikh Zayed Road and after crossing the Shahama area, take the exit for E10 – Sheikh Zayed bin Sultan Street. As soon as you cross Deerfields Mall, take the Yas Island exit, for E12 – Sheikh Khalifa bin Zayed Street, which will take you to Saadiyat Island, via a picturesque route that covers Yas Island, Fahid Island and Al Jubail Island. When coming from Abu Dhabi city, you can take the E12 route from Abu Dhabi corniche, that will lead you straight to Saadiyat Island’s cultural district. Free parking is available on site.

source_snapshot.title: UAE criminal clearance certificate 2026: How to apply online with the Ministry of Interior, fees and documents
source_snapshot.text: Dubai: Are you applying for a visit visa to a country you’ve never been to before, or getting verified for a new job? In Dubai, you will need a police clearance certificate , which verifies the holder has not been involved in any unlawful actions during time spent in the UAE. However, if you are a resident of other emirates – Abu Dhabi, Sharjah, Ajman, Ras Al Khaimah, Fujairah or Umm Al Quwain – you can use the Ministry of Interior’s (MOI) online portal to get a criminal clearance certificate, which serves the same purpose. Why do I need the certificate? Like a Dubai Police-issued police clearance certificate, the ‘criminal clearance certificate’ is commonly required for employment, immigration, visa applications, company licensing, renting property, adopting children and marriage. Applicants seeking residency in countries like Canada, Australia or the UK, must provide this certificate for every country in which, they have resided. Within the UAE, it may be required for certain visa changes, or when applying for long-term residency categories. Can I apply for the certificate even if I’m no longer a UAE resident? According to the MOI website, a relative or friend of a former resident can submit a request for the certificate in person, at the General Directorate of the Federal Criminal Police at the Ministry of Interior, or the General Department of Criminal Security at the Ministry of Interior. The following documents are required to apply: Copy of the applicant’s passport. Copy of the applicant’s old residence permit. Copy of the applicant’s Emirates ID. Two personal photographs. What documents do I need to apply for the certificate online? No special documents are required for UAE residents besides the Emirates ID and a valid passport. However, Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) citizens and visitors to the UAE are required to complete a fingerprinting procedure before the certificate is issued. Biometrics collection can be done at authorised service centres, like Tasheel, available across the UAE, or at Federal Authority for Identity, Citizenship, Customs & Port Security (ICP) Customer Happiness Centres. Once processed, the criminal clearance certificate is issued in Arabic and English, and is valid for 30 days from the date of issuance. How to apply for the criminal clearance certificate If you are based in the UAE, you can apply for the certificate online through the following steps: Visit MOI’s website – moi.gov.ae – or download the MOI UAE app from the Google Play Store or Apple App Store. Sign in using your UAE PASS. Click on ‘Services’. Under ‘Police Services’, select ‘Issuance of Criminal Clearance Certificate’. Fill out the form with your personal details, including full name, and passport information. Specify whether you wish to use the certificate in the UAE or a foreign country. If it is the latter, note that you will also need to have the certificate attested – you can do so via the Ministry of Foreign Affairs’ (MOFA) attestation services . Specify the purpose of the certificate, such as immigration, work, study, and so on. Pay the fees and select whether you would like to get the certificate couriered to you, issued digitally, or would like for it to be collected in person. If you select in-person pick-up, you will need to visit the Federal Criminal Police department at the MOI, or a police station for collection – the exact location will be specified in a notification message upon completion of the service. The processing time for this service is 24 hours. Fees : Service fees (for use within the country): Dh50 Service fees (for use outside the country): Dh100 Fingerprinting fees for visitors and GCC citizens: Dh50

source_snapshot.title: How to check if a website is a scam in the UAE: Use the free StaySafe tool from the Cyber Security Council
source_snapshot.text: Dubai: Did you find tickets to a sold-out concert on a website? Or unbelievably discounted airfares for your dream holiday destination? It’s worth checking if the website is legitimate or phony, via the UAE Cyber Security Council’s StaySafe website. Here’s how to check whether a website is fraudulent, and how to avoid being scammed. What is StaySafe? With online phishing and scams on the rise in an increasingly digital world, the UAE government has taken steps to protect online users in the country through an online tool called StaySafe. Launched by the UAE’s Cyber Security Council, in partnership with etisalat and the Global Anti-Scam Alliance, the tool is completely free to use. StaySafe allows users to check the credibility of any website, by rating it against a range of parameters. The tool checks links against several sources for you, to check for malware, phishing, or scams. The UAE Cyber Security Council cautions, however, that the sources are neither complete nor perfect, and advises netizens to do their own checks as well, in order to avoid falling victim to online scams. How does the tool work? Follow these steps to use the StaySafe online tool: Visit staysafe.csc.gov.ae/en. Enter the website link in the ‘Search’ section. Following your input, StaySafe uses a colour-coded system – from red, yellow and light green to dark green – to flag potential scams, and gives you a website reliability score. If the result is dark green, this means the website is reliable and you can proceed to use it. If the indicator turns red, this means the website has a high potential for fraud. Once the colour-coded results are provided, StaySafe also shows whether the website has been reported in the past, for phishing, and whether it has been registered with the local authorities, as well as details regarding how old it is. How do I conduct a check to see if a website is a scam or phishing site? From fake investment opportunities to fraudulent online stores, there are plenty of ways to be scammed online. The Cyber Security Council shared the following tips to help individuals gain the ability to spot online scams: Use common sense: If the price of a product on a website looks too good to be true, it likely comes with strings attached. The authorities advise thinking twice and double-checking. The easiest way to do this is to simply check out the same product at competing websites that you trust. If the difference in prices is huge, it’s a red flag. Check out social media links: Scammers know consumers often expect retailers to have a social media presence, and so they insert logos of social media platforms on their websites. Scratching beneath the surface often reveals non-functional links. If there are functioning social media accounts, take a quick look to see if there are any posts. Oftentimes, if the website is a scam, angry users will let you know. Check the small print: Scammers often use placeholder or rushed text in pages like ‘About Us’, ‘Terms & Conditions’, ‘Shipping Policy’ and ‘Return Policy’ to give the air of professionality. If you find that these pages don’t exist or are of poor quality, think twice about shopping on the website. Check if brand names are being misused: A lot of fraudulent retail sites use brand names in combination with words like ‘discounted’, ‘cheap’, ‘sale’ and even ‘free’ to get visitors via search engines. However, premium brands rarely or never put their products on sale or offer huge discounts. Likewise, most serious online stores sell multiple brands and do not deal in only one brand. Pay attention to the look and feel of these websites. Legitimate websites have high-quality logos and pictures. Fraudulent websites can appear unprofessional, with odd looking formatting or low-resolution pictures. Look for a working trustmark: Trustmarks are authentication symbols displayed on a website to show that it has passed an independent assessment, and complies with specific standards for privacy, security, quality or trade practices. However, scam websites may also use them without permission, in an attempt to mislead consumers. A way to see if the trustmark is real is to click on it – if the functionality is not working, it’s a red flag. Check the domain name: Certain websites will try and trick you into thinking they are the official websites of known brands, even if they have no relation to the actual company. Make sure that the domain name, or the link address, is as expected. For example, a real domain name of a brand may be ‘brand.com’, while a fake website might use variations like ‘brand.net’, or ‘brand.online’. Learn from reviews: A website using a well-known consumer review system is usually a good sign. However, some review systems are better than others. Check if the review system adheres to the Review Certification Standards, meaning the website cannot delete or edit reviews without proper cause. Websites like Scamadviser, TrustPilot and others allow users to leave review

source_snapshot.title: MOHRE urges caution over fake job offers, highlights five red flags
source_snapshot.text: The Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation (MOHRE) has warned job seekers against falling prey to fraudulent job offers, identifying five warning signs that warrant caution and verification before proceeding with any employment procedures. These signs include requests to open a bank account in the job seeker's name, requests to share bank account details, requests to pay employment fees, the use of the job seeker's bank account for receiving or transferring funds, and communication limited to messaging applications while refusing to use official channels. The latest data from the Labour Market Observatory shows that more than 2.6 million interactions with clients were recorded through various official channels during the third quarter of 2026. During the same period, the Ministry sent 27.4 million text messages and emails as part of its awareness campaigns and programmes, in addition to issuing approximately 7 million account statements to companies. The Ministry has identified five warning signs that should prompt job seekers to stop and verify before proceeding with employment. The first is a request to open a bank account in the job seeker's name . The Ministry urged caution when dealing with any employer that requests such a procedure as part of the recruitment process. The second warning sign is a request to share bank account details. The Ministry said job seekers should verify the identity of the employer and avoid sharing financial or banking information with untrusted entities or through unofficial channels. The third warning sign is a demand for payment in exchange for employment. The Ministry urged job seekers to stop and verify any request for payment related to a job offer and not proceed until they have confirmed the offer and the offering entity through official channels. The fourth warning sign is the use of the job seeker's bank account to receive or transfer funds. The Ministry said this is another red flag that requires caution and verification before complying with any such request, especially if it comes from an entity or individual contacting the job seeker outside official channels. The fifth warning sign is communication limited to messaging applications , with the entity refusing to provide any official means of contact or verify the job offer through approved channels. In such cases, job seekers are advised not to proceed with the hiring process until they have confirmed both the offer and the advertiser's identity. The Ministry emphasised the importance of verifying the employer and the job posting through its official channels before sharing any data or completing recruitment procedures. It noted that it can be contacted through its call centre on 600590000, via the MOHRE UAE application, or through its website. Data from the Ministry's Labour Market Observatory revealed a high level of reliance on its official communication channels during the third quarter of 2026. The call centre recorded 1,907,676 phone calls, while the Tawasul system, which includes email, chat and WhatsApp, recorded 351,594 interactions. The Customer Voice channel recorded 350,214 interactions during the same period. This brought the total number of interactions across the three channels to approximately 2.61 million during the third quarter of 2026, confirming the availability of multiple official channels for customers to verify information, make enquiries and provide feedback. The observatory's data also showed that 27,386,573 text messages and emails were sent as part of awareness campaigns and programmes during the third quarter. In addition, 3,773 business owners participated in the Customer First Forum sessions, while the Ministry held 26 customer council meetings within the forum during the same period. The Ministry recorded 51,098 communication transactions within the preferential services package for customers, while the number of account statements issued to companies reached 7,013,360 during the third quarter of this year.

source_snapshot.title: Heavy vehicle drivers must follow six safety rules under UAE's 2027 traffic regulations
source_snapshot.text: Dubai: Heavy trucks and heavy buses will be prohibited from overtaking one another within UAE cities under traffic regulations taking effect on January 1, 2027, which also establish requirements for vehicle loads, designated routes and drivers’ eyesight.The provisions are contained in Cabinet Decision No. 174 of 2026, which introduces the executive regulations of Federal Decree-Law No. 14 of 2024 on Traffic Regulation. .Get updated faster and for FREE: Download the Gulf News app now - simply click here..Under Article 34, heavy buses and heavy vehicles are prohibited from overtaking one another within cities. Outside urban areas, overtaking is permitted only if it does not obstruct traffic.The regulations also prohibit these vehicles from leaving designated lanes wherever such lanes are provided.Six obligations for heavy vehicle driversArticle 31 sets out six requirements that heavy vehicle drivers must follow.Drivers must remain on the right-hand side of the carriageway, leaving it only when necessary or when overtaking.They must also ensure that their vehicles do not exceed the load limits approved by the licensing authority or the permitted height restrictions.The regulations prohibit carrying passengers in heavy vehicles, except employees of the vehicle's owner and workers involved in loading and unloading, provided designated seats are available.Drivers must ensure that their cargo does not endanger the public or obstruct traffic. Loads such as sand and other loose materials must be covered to prevent dust or other substances from escaping or being blown from the vehicle.Cargo must also remain entirely within the vehicle's dimensions, with no part extending beyond its boundaries.Roads and timings for heavy vehiclesArticle 29 authorises licensing and traffic enforcement authorities, in coordination with the relevant government entities in each emirate, to determine the roads, lanes and times during which heavy vehicles are prohibited from operating.The same provision allows authorities to establish restrictions on the roads, lanes and operating hours of buses.These arrangements enable the relevant authorities in each emirate to determine where and when such vehicles may be restricted.Eyesight requirements for driversThe regulations also establish minimum eyesight standards for drivers seeking licences to operate heavy vehicles, taxis, buses and machinery.Under Article 62, applicants for heavy vehicle and taxi driving licences must meet one of two eyesight requirements:If vision in one eye is 6/6, vision in the other must range between 6/9 and 6/18.Alternatively, vision must be at least 6/9 in each eye.Applicants may meet these requirements with or without corrective lenses.Stricter requirements apply to drivers of light and heavy buses, as well as operators of light and heavy equipment and machinery.These applicants must have vision of at least 6/6 in each eye, with or without corrective lenses.The regulations also allow licensing authorities to accept eyesight examination reports issued outside the UAE when processing applications to renew expired driving licences.The measures form part of the executive regulations governing road use, driving licences and vehicle safety, which come into force across the UAE on January 1, 2027..UAE to limit driving to nine hours in 24-hour period under new traffic rules.UAE driving licence: 12 reasons it could be suspended, cancelled or not source_snapshot.title: RTA launches five-star performance rating system for taxi companies
source_snapshot.text: DUBAI, 15th November, 2026 (WAM) -- Dubai’s Roads and Transport Authority (RTA) has launched a five-star system to rate the performance of taxi companies in the emirate. The initiative aims to establish excellence in transport services, raise sector efficiency, improve the customer journey and encourage operators to adopt smart solutions and sustainable practices.Mattar Al Tayer, Director-General and Chairman of the Board of Executive Directors of RTA, affirmed that the system is a strategic tool for governing taxi service quality and building an integrated system for continuous improvement. It links incentives to performance results and enhances transparency and competitiveness among operators, strengthening the sector’s readiness to keep pace with growing demand and supporting Dubai’s transition towards smart and sustainable urban mobility.The assessment mechanism will be updated periodically, with company ratings displayed on the smart screens in taxis and at the entrance to each company’s headquarters. Companies awarded five stars will receive seven taxi plates, along with a certificate and a trophy from RTA, while four-star companies will receive five taxi plates. Measures aimed at improving performance and raising service levels will be applied to companies rated three stars or fewer.The assessment rests on four main pillars comprising 18 indicators. Sustainability covers electric and hydrogen vehicles, the ratio of drivers to vehicles, productive kilometres and average trip ratings. Technology measures e-hail bookings, electronic payments, driver management systems and implementation of the driver working-hours policy. Accountability covers serious traffic accidents, quality violations, complaints about reckless driving, customer satisfaction and driver satisfaction. Reliability covers vehicle availability, activation on the e-hail system and acceptance of e-hail requests during peak hours, as well as cleanliness.Dubai’s taxi sector comprises five companies: Dubai Taxi Company, Kabi Taxi, National Taxi, Arabia Taxi and Metro Taxi. In 2025, the total number of taxis exceeded 14,346 vehicles, of which 12,380 were electric or hybrid. evidence_passages.text: RTA launches five-star performance rating system for taxi companies
DUBAI, 15th November, 2026 (WAM) -- Dubai’s Roads and Transport Authority (RTA) has launched a five-star system to rate the performance of taxi companies in the emirate.

The initiative aims to establish excellence in transport services, raise sector efficiency, improve the customer journey and encourage operators to adopt smart solutions and sustainable practices.Mattar Al Tayer, Director-General and Chairman of the Board of Executive Directors of RTA, affirmed that the system is a strategic tool for governing taxi service quality and building an integrated system for continuous improvement.

It links incentives to performance results and enhances transparency and competitiveness among operators, strengthening the sector’s readiness to keep pace with growing demand and supporting Dubai’s transition towards smart and sustainable urban mobility.The assessment mechanism will be updated periodically, with company ratings displayed on the smart screens in taxis and at the entrance to each company’s headquarters.
Companies awarded five stars will receive seven taxi plates, along with a certificate and a trophy from RTA, while four-star companies will receive five taxi plates.
Measures aimed at improving performance and raising service levels will be applied to companies rated three stars or fewer.The assessment rests on four main pillars comprising 18 indicators.
Sustainability covers electric and hydrogen vehicles, the ratio of drivers to vehicles, productive kilometres and average trip ratings.
Technology measures e-hail bookings, electronic payments, driver management systems and implementation of the driver working-hours policy.
Accountability covers serious traffic accidents, quality violations, complaints about reckless driving, customer satisfaction and driver satisfaction.

Reliability covers vehicle availability, activation on the e-hail system and acceptance of e-hail requests during peak hours, as well as cleanliness.Dubai’s taxi sector comprises five companies: Dubai Taxi Company, Kabi Taxi, National Taxi, Arabia Taxi and Metro Taxi.

The share of hybrid vehicles in the fleet has exceeded 72 percent, while the transition to electric vehicles has reached 19 percent, exceeding the target set for 2026.
RTA is also expanding the testing and launch of electric autonomous vehicles in cooperation with major global companies, while developing infrastructure for fast-charging stations.

source_snapshot.title: Al Dhaid City entrance bridge opens to boost Central Region mobility
source_snapshot.text: SHARJAH, 16th November, 2026 (WAM) -- Under the directives of His Highness Sheikh Dr. Sultan bin Mohammed Al Qasimi, Supreme Council Member and Ruler of Sharjah, the Initiatives Implementation Authority (Mubadara) and the Sharjah Roads and Transport Authority, in collaboration with relevant entities in the emirate, inaugurated the Al Dhaid City entrance bridge on Monday morning.Spanning 320 metres, this milestone marks the completion of the first phase of the Al Dhaid Lake and Bridge project.Dr. Salah Butti Al Muhairi, Chairman of Mubadara, emphasised that Al Dhaid bridge and lake project is a comprehensive development initiative.It integrates the enhancement of the transport network, the expansion of water reserves, and the increase of green spaces—all of which serve to improve the quality of life and support sustainable development in the Central Region.Dr. Al Muhairi added that this vital project focuses on two primary pillars. The first involves the development of the road network and traffic flow; the Al Dhaid Bridge has been expanded to four lanes in each direction, covering a total length of approximately one kilometre, with an underpass spanning 320 metres and a capacity of up to 6,000 vehicles per hour.To ensure the highest standards of traffic safety and smooth movement, the design separates truck lanes from those for light vehicles.The bridge serves as a crucial artery connecting several residential and key areas within the city—including Tal Al Zafaran, Taiba, Jebel Omar, and Al Sharia—thereby facilitating travel for residents and visitors alike and reducing transit times.He explained that the second component of the project involves developing the water and environmental ecosystem beneath the bridge. This includes the creation of a 2.3-kilometre-long lake, designed to serve as a strategic water reserve as well as a recreational and sports destination.It features family seating areas, parks, and dedicated paths for pedestrians and cyclists. The lake has been designed and prepared to accommodate water sports—most notably rowing—thereby providing a significant, high-quality addition to the city’s sports and tourism facilities.The Chairman of Mubadara revealed that the project design incorporates a 2.3-kilometre-long, 24-metre-wide water channel intended to manage wadi (valley) runoff and protect both the bridge and the lake.This channel is preceded by three collection lakes designed to reduce the intensity of flash floods and facilitate groundwater recharge. These measures ensure the sustainability of the facilities, protecting them from adverse weather conditions and the force of wadi flows by allowing water to percolate into the ground.Al Muhairi highlighted the project’s environmental significance, noting that it adds a unique aesthetic and climatic dimension to the entrance of Al Dhaid city.This is achieved through expansive green spaces surrounding the lake, as well as a forest project—commissioned by the Ruler of Sharjah—that extends from the end of the lake toward the Khorfakkan Road.Together, these elements expand the city’s green cover, promote eco-friendly features, and solidify Al Dhaid’s status as a green oasis that harmoniously blends the authenticity of nature with modern infrastructure.

source_snapshot.title: Dubai bans teachers from using personal phones, social media accounts to contact students
source_snapshot.text: Dubai: Can teachers in Dubai use their personal mobile phones, WhatsApp or social media accounts to communicate with students?Under new safeguarding requirements introduced by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority (KHDA), staff at private educational institutions are prohibited from using personal devices, private contact details or social media platforms to communicate with learners.Instead, all teaching and communication must take place through institutionally approved devices and platforms.The restrictions are part of KHDA's new Policy Framework for Safeguarding and Learner Protection in Dubai’s Private Educational Institutions, announced on November 13.The framework establishes common safeguarding standards across Dubai's private education sector, including rules on professional conduct, reporting concerns and protecting learners from harm..What communication is prohibited?Under the framework's section on Professional Conduct and Safe Working Practice, institutions must:“Prohibit personal or secretive relationships with learners, use of private contact details, and use of personal devices or social media for communication with learners.”“Require communication and teaching to take place only through institutionally approved devices and platforms.”In practice, this means teachers and other staff cannot use their personal WhatsApp accounts, private phone numbers or social media profiles to communicate with students. Instead, communication must remain within the institution's approved channels, where appropriate safeguards and oversight can be maintained..Dubai schools must report students absent for five consecutive days under new rules.What other restrictions apply to teachers and staff?The new framework also establishes professional boundaries governing how adults interact with learners, both online and in person.Institutions must ensure staff:Do not accept unauthorised gifts or show preferential treatment to particular learners.Follow rules on photography, social media and digital content involving students.Work in visible, open environments wherever practicable.Follow documented supervision and safeguarding arrangements when one-to-one or closed-door interactions are necessary.Institutions must also monitor staff suitability throughout employment and take appropriate action when concerns arise..Dubai schools can temporarily suspend staff over student safety concerns under new rules.Who must follow the new rules?The framework applies beyond private school teachers.It covers KHDA-permitted private educational institutions across Dubai, including:Early childhood centres and nurseriesPrivate schoolsUniversities and higher education institutionsVocational and training institutesThe requirements extend to physical campuses and virtual learning environments.All adults working with learners, including coaches, volunteers and third-party contractors, must acknowledge the institution's Code of Conduct during induction.Safeguarding responsibilities also extend to learners aged 18 and above, with procedures adapted to adult consent and confidentiality..How is the new framework different?While many private educational institutions in Dubai already had safeguarding policies in place, KHDA's new framework introduces a unified set of mandatory standards across the sector.These standards cover preventing and identifying harm, handling allegations, reporting safeguarding concerns and ensuring accountability. They also address risks such as cyberbullying, online grooming, digital coercion and the misuse of artificial intelligence.Institutions must also appoint a safeguarding governor at board level and a designated safeguarding lead or child protection coordinator to oversee safeguarding responsibilities.By requiring staff to use approved communication channels and maintain clear professional boundaries, the new policy aims to reduce the risk of inappropriate contact with learners and ensure safeguarding concerns are properly identified and reported..When do the new rules take effect?The framework has been introduced with a phased implementation period of up to 12 months, allowing institutions to update policies, train staff and review safeguarding procedures.The requirements form part of KHDA's wider effort to establish consistent learner protection standards across Dubai's private education sector..Dubai bans Arabic teachers from teaching Islamic Education without separate KHDA approval.What Dubai schools should prepare for KHDA’s 24-hour notice inspections.CBSE exams 2027: UAE schools step up preparations as students raise concerns over exam schedules.No homework for 10 years: What UAE private schools have learnt about children's progress
