source_snapshot.title: Dubai launches AI tool that reads your Google reviews to catch food safety risks early
source_snapshot.text: Dubai: The next time you post a Google review about a meal out in Dubai, it could do more than guide fellow diners. Dubai Municipality on Monday launched intelSPECT, an artificial intelligence-powered tool that reads customer reviews of restaurants and food establishments across the emirate to spot food safety problems early.The name is short for "intelligently inspect". The tool was unveiled at the 20th Dubai International Food Safety Conference (DIFSC), which runs from November 16 to 18 at the Dubai World Trade Centre.It is one of multiple initiatives showcased at the event, all part of a new roadmap announced under the theme "The new era of intelligent food systems"..Get updated faster and for FREE: Download the Gulf News app now - simply click here..Dr Naseem Mohammed Rafee, Acting CEO of the Environment, Health and Safety Agency at Dubai Municipality, told Gulf News the system uses a risk-based approach, letting the municipality categorise areas of Dubai by risk, identify where non-compliance is higher, and prioritise inspections and corrective action..Dubai has a new radar, this time to flag health and safety risks. "Essentially, we are moving from a reactive approach to a proactive one," she said. "Rather than waiting for an incident to occur, we can use customer feedback to identify potential problem areas and take preventive action."How it worksThe AI scrapes what customers post on Google and continuously analyses it for warning signs. When a trend emerges, such as one type of cuisine or a particular group of restaurants drawing similar complaints, officials look for the common link. Those findings then help guide where inspections should focus.Speaking about the project at the municipality's stall, Bobby Krishna, Principal Food Safety Specialist at the Food Safety Department of Dubai Municipality and a member of the International Commission on Microbiological Specifications for Foods (ICMSF), said intelSPECT is not a complaint-monitoring system. It is designed for foresight, helping the authority detect problems in different areas in advance..Dubai launches A-to-E food rating system to help shoppers make healthier choices. "It uses insights from Google reviews and other data sources to forecast potential food safety risks, enabling authorities to take preventive action before problems arise," he said.For diners, that means problems can be tackled at their root. If restaurants serving a particular type of fish are being affected, for instance, the municipality can trace where that fish comes from and act. The tool also checks how businesses respond to reported problems; if issues are not corrected, the municipality can issue instructions.Spotting the signsPropAI, the company behind the tool, said it is based on the Dubai Food Code by the municipality. It scans for pest activity, food contamination, suspected foodborne illness or food poisoning, cleanliness issues and improper food preparation.A PropAI representative said none of the reviews are treated as established facts; they are simply indicators that an establishment may need to be checked. The municipality has also clarified that the tool can work out whether someone is maliciously targeting a restaurant, while helping businesses tackle genuine issues.PropAI acknowledged that fake reviews exist and said Google already has systems to flag them, while it is developing its own capabilities. “We believe it is better to have more information than to overlook potentially important feedback."The tool is not meant to replace human inspectors. For now, it helps management and inspection teams decide which restaurants to prioritise on a particular day, rather than waiting until the following week.The municipality’s message to consumers is to speak up. Official channels exist to report issues directly to Dubai Municipality, and feedback on Google and other platforms, including positive comments, is now more valuable.Roadmap and toolsThe Roadmap for the Future of Food Safety in Dubai covers innovation, artificial intelligence, partnerships and food safety, among other priorities. "Over the next three years, this roadmap will guide us into a new era of food safety, supported by advanced technologies and innovative approaches," Dr Naseem said.One of the initiatives, inSIGHT uses AI-based technology and digital tools to flag potential food safety risks, including microbial risks on surfaces, particularly in manufacturing facilities.A real-time detection device named CSI developed by SafetySpec lets inspectors and operators scan surfaces to find contamination invisible to the naked eye, with different substances appearing in different colours. It does not identify specific pathogens but works as an initial screening tool to locate hotspots for further testing under established protocols.The Kikkoman hygiene monitoring system, developed in Japan, includes a scanner for analysing Easy Plate (pre-prepared film media) samples used in environmental hygiene testing, and Bioglo, a UV-based device that detects biofilms on surfaces. Smart glasses record where and when inspections are conducted. These devices were among the tools displayed by Biomed Healthcare Trading.Meanwhile, HealthyfAi is an educational platform integrating learning resources, food chain information and technology.

source_snapshot.title: UAE vegetable prices fall by up to 42% as local farm produce reaches shelves
source_snapshot.text: Dubai: Vegetable markets have begun to record declines in the prices of a number of items. The trend comes with the start of the local agricultural season and the introduction of Emirati crops to sales outlets, which has boosted supply and contributed to a decrease in price limits for some vegetables by about 42%, in addition to offering extensive deals on other items. The decline was observed in the price limits of certain vegetables at retail outlets, most notably zucchini; its displayed price reached Dh6.95 per kilogram, compared to a previous price of Dh12, a decrease of 42%. Meanwhile, the price for green pepper varieties reached about Dh9 per kilogram, compared to a previous price that of Dh11, with a decrease of about 18%. The price of cucumbers also decreased to Dh4 per kilogram, compared to Dh6 previously, a decrease of 33%, while the price of eggplant reached about Dh6.95 dirhams per kilogram, compared to Dh7.95 previously, a decrease of 12.6%. The outlets witnessed various offers, most notably on varieties of tomatoes, potatoes and lemons. The downward trend in prices comes with the start of the local agricultural season and the introduction of Emirati crops to sales outlets. File photograph Vegetable traders and suppliers said that the introduction of varieties of local seasonal vegetables has raised the levels of price competition and given consumers wider choices at more competitive prices. It has also contributed to lowering the prices of a variety of vegetables available in the market, which previously relied more heavily on products supplied from foreign markets. This, in turn, has provided greater options with lower prices for consumers, supported an increase in supply in the markets, and led to greater discounts on vegetables. The outlets pointed out that the local supply will increase even more during December 2026 and January 2027, which will enhance price reductions and offers. The CEO of NRTC Group, which supplies vegetables and fruits, Muhammad Nassar Al-Rifai, said that “the introduction of varieties from the local agricultural season supported the decline in price limits for varieties traded in the markets, and supported the introduction of different price offers in sales outlets.” He stressed that “the increasing supply of local agricultural produce will support market stability and lower price limits, especially during the peak of local vegetable production in January,” noting that “local agricultural produce, with the diversity of supply from different markets, enhances the abundance of supply and stabilises price limits for different types of vegetables in the markets.” CEO of NRTC Group Muhammad Nassar Al-Rifai said that “the introduction of varieties from the local agricultural season supported the decline in price limits." Picture credit: Supplied Issa Najib Al-Khoury, CEO of Mirak Food and Vegetable Supply Company, said that “the markets have recently witnessed the introduction of varieties of vegetables from the local agricultural season, which in turn has contributed to reducing the price limits of the varieties of vegetables available in the markets, and raising the levels of offers offered in the sales outlets.” He explained that “the introduction of local agricultural season products is still in its early stages, and the introduction processes will gradually increase at higher rates, especially during December 2026 and January 2027, which in turn will enhance the availability of low prices for various vegetables and increase the rates of offers on them.” Vegetable trader Mohammed Aziz said: “The markets are witnessing a decrease in the prices of currently available vegetable varieties with the start of introducing local agricultural season products into the markets, which has made available varieties with lower price limits compared to previous periods that relied more on products supplied from foreign markets, and therefore the options were limited, and prices were determined by the countries of origin and according to the cost of shipping and transportation and operational variables.” He added: “The supply of locally grown vegetables is expected to increase in the coming weeks in the markets, and more so compared to last year, as a number of local farms move to increase production and offer it through sales outlets via supply contracts.” Vegetable trader Muhammad Qasim pointed out that “the introduction of new varieties from the agricultural season during the recent period has had a positive impact on the markets through the decline in the price limits of the vegetables available in general in the markets compared to previous periods, which was evident through basic vegetable varieties such as cucumbers and zucchini.” He explained that “the increased supply of vegetables in the markets following the introduction of local varieties has raised the rates of offers on vegetable prices, and reduced the price limits for the types of vegetables available in the markets.”

source_snapshot.title: UAE traffic regulations 2027: Rules truck, bus and school bus drivers must follow
source_snapshot.text: Dubai: Truck drivers and buses in the UAE will have a new set of driving regulations to follow from next year as the UAE is set to implement Cabinet Decision No. 174 of 2026 from January 1, 2027. The Decision covers various aspects that affect heavy goods vehicles and buses, however, not all the rules stipulated for truck and bus drivers may be entirely new. Zeiad Yehia, Legal Director at Al-Mur Law Firm, said: “Cabinet Decision No. 174 of 2026 ...introduces a comprehensive new executive regulatory framework for road traffic in the UAE. “The Resolution comprises 131 articles and comes into force on January 1, 2027. It implements Federal Decree-Law No. 14 of 2024 on the Regulation of Traffic, which itself came into force on March 29, 2025." Zeiad Yehia, Legal Director at Al-Mur Law Firm So, what does the new legislation say about the responsibilities of truck and bus drivers? Here’s all you need to know. Stopping in residential areas As per Article 17 (6), heavy vehicles or vehicles carrying heavy machinery and equipment must not stop in residential areas , unless they are parked for construction or development purposes. The law also requires the licensing and traffic authorities within each emirate to specify any roads, routes and timings during which heavy goods vehicles are prohibited from travelling. Overtaking rules Article 34 of the law also specifies that heavy buses and heavy goods vehicles should not overtake one another within city limits or near city borders, unless doing so does not obstruct traffic flow on the road. Also, in cases where there are designated lanes for heavy vehicles, drivers must not deviate from them. Six obligations of truck drivers Drivers of heavy goods vehicles should also follow these six rules at all times: 1. Stay on the right-most lane and not leave it unless necessary or when overtaking. 2. Ensure that the load on the truck does not exceed the load limit set by the licensing authority or the permitted height of the load. 3. Drivers cannot carry any passengers in heavy goods vehicles, except for the vehicle owner’s employees and loading and unloading staff, provided there are seats designated for them. 4. The vehicle’s load should not pose a danger to the public or obstruct traffic. 5. A cover must be fitted to prevent dust and other articles, such as sand, from leaking or being blown away from the truck load. 6. The load must not protrude beyond the vehicle’s dimensions in any way. Payload rules Article 37 of the Resolution also requires the driver to ensure that the payload is organised and arranged in a way that it is secure and fastened to the vehicle at all times and does not pose any danger to people or property. The load must also not obstruct the driver’s view, or obscure any hand signals, light signals, direction indicators, vehicle lights, mirrors or number plates. Passenger transport buses Article 33 of the Resolution also requires buses to have prominent signage indicating that it is authorised to carry paying passengers and the number of passengers permitted on the bus. Owners of the buses should also display a copy of the approved fare schedule in prominent places inside the bus or carry it on the bus so that it can be shown on request. Responsibilities of bus drivers Bus drivers must also ensure the following: The number of passengers does not exceed the limit authorised on the bus licence. Passengers must not stick their heads, hands or any part of their bodies out of the windows. The interior of the bus must be lit between sunset and sunrise, and whenever necessary. They do not stop to pick up or drop off passengers except at authorised locations. They do not speak to passengers while the bus is moving and not allow passengers to stand or sit next to them. They not refuse to carry any person who is willing to pay the prescribed fare, provided that the bus is not full. To inspect the vehicle right after the end of each journey, check for any items that may have been left behind and hand them over to the nearest police station within 24 hours. The police station must provide proof of this handover of item. School bus drivers When picking up and dropping off school pupils, drivers must ensure the following: They must park the vehicle parallel to the kerb in areas where it is permitted. Switch on the front and rear indicators. Open the side ‘stop’ indicator arm. Motorists must ensure that they come to a complete stop when they see a school bus stopped in such a manner. For two-way roads, vehicles in both directions must come to a complete stop and for roads that have a divider, vehicles in the same direction as a bus must come to a complete stop.

source_snapshot.title: Dubai Marina Vertiport completed, certified to handle 84,000 passengers annually
source_snapshot.text: DUBAI, 18th November, 2026 (WAM) -- Skyports Infrastructure, in collaboration with Dubai's Roads and Transport Authority (RTA), has completed Dubai Marina Vertiport, which has received official certification from the General Civil Aviation Authority (GCAA) for commercial electric vertical take-off and landing (eVTOL) operations.Designated VMR, the facility enables the world's first permanent electric air taxi route between two vertiports, connecting Dubai Marina with VDX, the network's primary vertiport near Dubai International Airport.The route will be operated by Joby Aviation using electric aircraft designed for urban environments, featuring low noise levels, zero operating emissions and speeds of up to 200 miles per hour.The service is expected to reduce travel time between the two facilities to less than 10 minutes, compared with approximately 35 minutes by road. Commercial operations will begin once the necessary operational approvals and readiness requirements are completed.Joby Aviation has been conducting piloted electric air taxi test flights in Dubai since June 2025. In November of the same year, the company completed the UAE's first point-to-point air taxi flight, connecting its testing facility in Margham with Al Maktoum International Airport.Dubai Marina Vertiport is the second completed and certified facility in the Dubai Air Taxi network, following VDX, under the GCAA's CAR AGA Part VFI regulations.Located next to the American University in Dubai and within walking distance of Al Fardan Exchange Metro Station, the facility will support multimodal connectivity between Dubai Marina's residential and entertainment areas, Dubai Internet City's business and technology districts, and the wider public transport network.The vertiport can accommodate up to 21,000 landings and 84,000 passengers annually.Its infrastructure includes a passenger terminal, an aircraft charging facility and a single elevated touchdown and lift-off area (TLOF), alongside a dedicated aircraft parking area that enables another aircraft to continue operations without obstruction.The facility incorporates design standards commonly used in offshore aviation infrastructure, under GCAA supervision, to enhance safety, operational efficiency and structural resilience.Two additional vertiports are being developed in Downtown Dubai and Palm Jumeirah, forming part of the initial Dubai Air Taxi network.Ahmed Bahrozyan, CEO of the Corporate Technology Support Services Sector at RTA and Chairman of the Autonomous Transport and Aerial Taxi Committee, said the completion and certification of Dubai Marina Vertiport represent a significant step towards developing an integrated, smart and sustainable mobility system.He emphasised that the new transport service will complement Dubai's existing public transport network and enhance connectivity between key destinations across the emirate.Aqeel Ahmed Al Zarouni, Assistant Director-General for Aviation Safety Affairs at the GCAA, said having two certified vertiports in Dubai strengthens the UAE's readiness to develop an advanced air mobility ecosystem within a regulatory framework prioritising safety and cooperation between government entities, regulators and industry partners.Addison Ferrell, Director at Skyports Infrastructure, described the certification of both facilities as a global milestone in transforming advanced air mobility into a practical reality through collaboration between Skyports, RTA, Joby Aviation and the GCAA.Anthony El-Khoury, General Manager of Joby Aviation in the UAE, said the company is progressing with operational testing and commissioning of the vertiports using its aircraft in preparation for launching commercial services.He noted that the service will significantly reduce travel times to and from the airport, with plans to expand the network to additional destinations across Dubai.

source_snapshot.title: UAE school exam cheating: Zero grade, 12 conduct points lost and no make-up exam, schools warn
source_snapshot.text: Dubai: A number of schools have warned that cheating or helping others to cheat could result in a zero grade in the subject, a deduction of 12 points from conduct, and disqualification from the make-up exam, ahead of the start of the end-of-first-semester exams for the 2026-2027 academic year, scheduled for November 25 for students from grades three to twelve. The anti-cheating regulations specify seven prohibitions for students, including: Using mobile phones or social media during the exam. Exchanging conversations, signals, or any form of communication between students inside the hall. Looking at or copying other people’s answers. Leaking questions or participating in distributing them. Intentionally damaging the exam paper or the contents of the hall. Impersonating others in school transactions or when entering exam halls. Using external parties to accomplish learning or project-based assessment tasks. The Ministry of Education's guidelines classify cheating as a serious offence. If a student is caught cheating, they receive zero marks in the subject in which the violation occurred. If the violation is proven for the first time, 12 points are deducted from their conduct grade, they are barred from taking the make-up exam, and their guardian is notified of the decision. If cheating is repeated, whether via using social media or any other means, the student receives zero marks in all subjects within Group A and is referred to a behavioural modification program in cooperation with their guardian, in addition to the penalties stipulated in the code of conduct. The procedures extend to cases captured by cameras. If a photo or video shows a student cheating, they will receive zero marks on the exam and be subject to the prescribed disciplinary action. Guidelines for cases captured by cameras stipulate a zero in all subjects for repeated offences. The school investigates the incident, documents its details in a dedicated form, informs the student of what has been recorded against him/her, then refers the case to the relevant authority, and involves the parent in the procedures taken. The Ministry stressed that allowing or assisting students to cheat is a serious violation of the code of conduct, which warrants holding the teacher accountable. It indicated that it is taking the necessary measures to monitor the progress of exams in schools, and to detect and follow up on cases of cheating.

source_snapshot.text: Dubai: Passports are no longer just for people. Dubai is set to give them to the materials that build the city, starting with steel, aluminium and cement, in an attempt to extend their journey in supporting a circular economy.At Dubai Future Week 2026, which opened on Wednesday Dubai Municipality revealed to Gulf News that Building Materials Passport will be released at the beginning of 2027.It will be mandatory for everyone in the emirate’s construction industry, including all manufacturers and suppliers, to comply, said Salama Al Suwaidi, architectural engineer at the Building Permits Department, Dubai Municipality, who presented the project at Emirates Towers..Get updated faster and for FREE: Download the Gulf News app now - simply click here..How the passport worksEach material that leaves the laboratory will have its own number, information and specifications recorded in a central system managed by the municipality. Manufacturers or suppliers must apply through the system and provide the technical details.The municipality then issues the passport based on that information. If the details do not match the required standards, the material is deemed invalid.Cement from different companies, for instance, will each carry a different passport.A life cycle that does not endUntil now, the industry has followed a linear model: materials are bought, used in construction and, once a building is demolished, taken to landfill. The new passport system is designed to turn that into a circular economy.After demolition, materials will be taken to laboratories and tested. Al Suwaidi gave the example of steel found to have 50 per cent of its strength. It would be fortified and treated so it can be used again as a new material in new buildings, an upcycling process."It's a life cycle that does not end," she said. It stops only when a material, such as a steel column, is no longer usable and must go to landfill for safety reasons.Nowhere to hideThe passport will also let authorities track what happened to specific materials after a building comes down. Those responsible for a building will be asked to account for the materials on its list of passports, including why something was not recycled after demolition. All recyclable materials from demolition sites will have to be recycled.The aims are to reduce reliance on imported materials, cut costs, lower carbon emissions and make construction more sustainable.In the initial phase, the system will cover just the three materials, but Al Suwaidi said the ambition is to target everything eventually.Dubai Future Week 2026, organised by the Dubai Future Foundation, runs till November 21 at Emirates Towers and the Museum of the Future. source_snapshot.title: Dubai Civil Defence announces colour-coded AI safety platform for buildings and more drones for firefighting
source_snapshot.text: Dubai: Dubai Civil Defence is set to give property investors a live, colour-coded view of how safe their buildings are, and plans to expand its firefighting drone fleet from two to six by next year, officials told Gulf News at Dubai Future Week on Thursday.The new digital platform, called Safety Pulse for Investors, will launch in the first quarter of 2027. Authorities say it is the first of its kind in the Middle East.It uses artificial intelligence (AI) and Internet of Things (IoT) technology to feed real-time safety data directly to owners and investors..Get updated faster and for FREE: Download the Gulf News app now - simply click here..How it worksUntil now, the safety data on Dubai's buildings was held by Civil Defence and linked to its operations room. Now it will be shared with those who own the buildings. Investors will see everything on one dashboard. They can pass it on to their operations or maintenance engineers, who will no longer have to chase information.Each building will be colour-coded, with green signalling a healthy rating. The rating depends on factors such as maintenance records, false alarms, defects in safety systems, missed inspections and the absence of a Civil Defence safety certificate. AI will help categorise the data..Abu Dhabi deploys AI-Driven drones as first responders to emergencies and disasters.The platform tracks five systems: fire alarms, firefighting equipment, gas, electrical and lifts. It can spot faults, leaks and maintenance needs early. It can also connect owners with maintenance companies and send alerts to the Civil Defence Operations Room without human intervention.The platform is linked to all 26 fire and rescue stations in the emirate, with plans to grow to 40 stations and points in line with the Dubai 2040 Urban Master Plan.Investors will be able to see the nearest station to their property, while Civil Defence teams can anticipate incidents and speed up their response. Investors with many properties can analyse the safety risks in multiple buildings at the same time and can take preventive or corrective measures.The Safety Pulse Platform covers investment and commercial properties but not private homes. Integration with Dubai Municipality and free zone licensing data is possible in future.Safety as an economic asset“Safety and investment are two sides of the same coin,” said Afaf Jassim Al Muhairi, CEO of the General Department of Institutional Leadership and Excellence at Dubai Civil Defence. She said the aim is to move from traditional supervision to proactive prevention, protecting investments as well as lives.Lt Col Eng Taher Hassan Al Taher, director of the corporate pioneership department, said the data matters because investors need to know where they are putting their money. “He doesn’t have to ask or look for information. He will have everything on one platform,” he said..Sharjah’s Aman system monitors 13,700 buildings for fire alerts.The announcement also includes a Global Attractiveness Index, which measures how safety affects investor and tourist decisions. It rests on four pillars: future readiness (30 per cent), proactive safety (25 per cent), protection of lives and property (20 per cent) and business continuity (25 per cent).Al Taher said safety, of buildings and of places, is one of the reasons tourists and investors choose Dubai. The platform is also expected to use AI and digital twins to predict risks.More Shaheen dronesOn firefighting, Al Taher said Civil Defence currently has two Shaheen drones and expects to have six by next year, “hopefully” with updated features.The Shaheen is Dubai Civil Defence’s AI-powered firefighting drone system for high-rise buildings. It was unveiled at Intersec 2025. It carries 1,200 litres of water and firefighting foam and is designed for buildings up to 200 metres tall.It was used in September 2025 to help bring a residential building fire in Al Barsha under control. Civil Defence crews reached the scene within six minutes and no injuries were reported. An improved version was showcased in January 2026.The new features are still in research and development and will be announced later. For now, the drones are meant for high-rise buildings. The aim is to eventually reach interiors as well.Asked about challenges, Al Taher said Civil Defence is prepared and ready for any critical situation. He said no policy changes were needed after when Dubai faced attacks as part of the regional crisis, as such scenarios were already factored in.

source_snapshot.title: GDRFA Dubai shifts Humanitarian Cases Section from November 23
source_snapshot.text: Dubai: Dubai’s Humanitarian Cases Section will relocate to Dubai International Airport from November 23, with all services moving temporarily to an alternative facility while maintenance work is carried out at its Dubai Festival City premises. The General Directorate of Identity and Foreigners Affairs (GDRFA) Dubai announced on Friday that the section will remain closed at its current location from Monday, November 23, until Saturday, January 30, 2027..Get updated faster and for FREE: Download the Gulf News app now - simply click here..During the temporary closure, all services and responsibilities will be transferred to the free zone section at Dubai International Airport in Al Twar 2, allowing customers to continue accessing services without disruption. The alternative centre will receive customers from November 23 during the approved working hours of 6.30am to 2.30pm, and from 6.30am to noon on Fridays. The timings exclude official public holidays.GDRFA Dubai said it had put all necessary operational arrangements in place to ensure a smooth transfer and equipped the alternative premises to accommodate customers and meet their needs.The authority stressed that the temporary relocation would not affect service delivery, with existing standards of efficiency and quality maintained throughout the maintenance period.Customers seeking assistance from the Humanitarian Cases Section have been urged to visit the free zone section at Dubai International Airport in Al Twar 2 from November 23, instead of heading to the closed Dubai Festival City premises.The GDRFA also said its Google Maps listing for the original location would be updated to show the status as "Temporarily Closed", together with details of the alternative service location and its working hours.The authority reaffirmed its commitment to keeping customers updated through its official communication channels.For enquiries and further information, customers can contact the Amer Call Centre on 8005111..GDRFA Dubai announces holiday working hours for Prophet’s Birthday.Dubai Eid Al Fitr: GDRFA working hours announced.GDRFA Dubai announces Ramadan 2026 working hours.GDRFA Dubai brings services closer to residents at Global Village
